Use the following as the implementation contract.

1. **Source drift:** Pin production to Box2D v3.1.1, released 2025-06-04 at commit `8c661469c9507d3ad6fbd2fea3f1aa71669c2fe3`, make its tagged public headers authoritative because website Doxygen remains at 3.1.0, and reject symbols absent from that pin. Current `main` commit `617d32ab02570930625bbcb8479f54be9bf8d045` identifies 3.2.0 and contains experimental snapshot, recording, state-hash, runtime-worker, and additional CCD APIs that must not enter the adapter. Remove 2.4 C++ pointers, fixtures, listeners, object traversal, and iteration-pair `Step` overloads, record source-tree, public-header, library, compiler, architecture, CMake, floating-point, and adapter hashes, and require an adapter compile/link probe against the pinned artifact on Windows and Linux.

2. **ID ownership:** Initialize definitions with `b2DefaultWorldDef`, `b2DefaultBodyDef`, `b2DefaultShapeDef`, and `b2DefaultChainDef`, expose durable application IDs to gameplay, and keep opaque generational Box2D IDs only inside adapter mappings whose validity ends at the documented destruction cascade or tick-boundary command. `IsValid` checks protect access for up to 64K allocations and do not provide durable identity, world destruction invalidates all bodies, shapes, and joints, body destruction invalidates attached shapes and joints, and chain or owning-body destruction invalidates segment shape IDs. Normalize arbitrary destruction requests into tick-boundary commands, invalidate every affected mapping before later gameplay processing, never retain a raw ID in a queued event, and test randomized create, destroy, recreate, body cascade, chain cascade, joint cascade, and destruction-generated events. Make mass changes explicit through `b2DestroyShape(shapeId, updateBodyMass)` or `b2Body_ApplyMassFromShapes`, account for sensor mass, and recreate rather than mutate a shape when changing sensor status.

3. **Step and tasks:** Run `b2World_Step` on a fixed simulation tick independent of the 48–240 Hz renderer, choose fixed substeps and a fixed worker configuration from a measured correctness-cost matrix, and reject render-delta replay or adaptive substeps as simulation inputs. Sweep candidate tick rates such as 60, 90, and 120 Hz, substeps 1, 2, 4, and 8, and workers 1, 2, 4, and the proposed production count on the 2,000-shape scene plus adversarial scenes, measuring at least 10,000 post-warmup ticks and recording p50, p95, p99, maximum step time, `b2World_GetProfile`, `b2World_GetCounters`, solver and task costs, contact counts, event counts, and correctness failures. Select the cheapest configuration with no declared stability failures and p99 within the 3 ms CPU budget, freeze it in replay metadata, and drive rendering with accumulator/interpolation without changing physics cadence. A nonserial `workerCount` requires `enqueueTask` and `finishTask`, `b2World_Step` is an exclusive locked phase, and task or collision callbacks must be bounded, thread-safe, world-read-free, world-write-free, and limited to immutable inputs plus indexed or thread-local outputs joined before outside-step work.

4. **Events and sensors:** Opt in to body, sensor, and contact events only where needed, drain the borrowed arrays from `b2World_GetBodyEvents`, `b2World_GetSensorEvents`, and `b2World_GetContactEvents` after every main step before mutation or another step, and immediately copy scalars while resolving raw IDs to durable application IDs. End-touch events can be caused by destruction and can contain destroyed IDs, so `b2Shape_IsValid` is only an access guard and gameplay identity comes from the adapter’s mapping and destruction commands. Build persistent trigger overlaps from transient begin and end events, support sensor-to-sensor pairs, canonicalize event kind and application-ID order before priority resolution or hashing, and test begin, stay, end, destruction-end, sensor-sensor, simultaneous events, and creation-order permutations. Replace “any contact this frame” grounding with a persistent support set keyed by durable shape pairs and qualified by solver contact normal, role, relative motion, and the current fixed tick.

5. **Queries:** Treat `b2World_OverlapAABB`, `b2World_OverlapShape`, rays, and shape casts as immediate outside-step observations, collect and copy all relevant hits, and sort multiple hits by fraction and durable identity before gameplay use. `b2World_OverlapAABB` returns approximate broadphase candidates, so require `b2World_OverlapShape` or explicit narrow-phase geometry for actual overlap. World casts can report a starts-inside result with zero fraction, zero normal, and an arbitrary point, which must be handled as a distinct state rather than interpreted as a support surface. Use queries for probes, anticipation, recovery diagnostics, and fast-crossing detection rather than as persistent contacts, and test starts-inside, equal-fraction hits, reversed creation order, broadphase false positives, thin geometry, and moving targets.

6. **PreSolve:** Implement one-way solids by setting `enablePreSolveEvents` only on relevant dynamic shapes and deciding in `b2PreSolveFcn` before resolution using immutable precomputed context, with the contact disabled again on every qualifying step. Disabling a contact after `b2World_Step` is too late, contacts re-enable during collision processing, and the parallel callback cannot read or mutate the world. Qualify using approach side, previous foot position, platform-relative velocity, drop-through state, translating or rotating platform motion, spawn overlap, and a validated speed and thickness envelope. Stable v3.1.1 warns that this PreSolve technique may pause and does not work for high-speed collisions, so crossings outside the proven envelope must follow an explicit policy such as pass-through or a separately validated cast-driven controller path, and the official Platformer sample is only a seed for tests covering jump-through, landing, underside contact, drop-through, spawn overlap, platform reversal, rotation, and fast crossing.

7. **Character mover:** Choose the solver-driven physical capsule as the initial production contract for characters that must ride moving platforms and interact physically, keep it integrated through forces or velocities and qualified contacts, and prohibit post-ray teleport correction or any hybrid that combines body contacts with geometric depenetration. Drive moving platforms with fixed-tick physical motion rather than render-time teleports, track the supporting platform by durable identity, and evaluate support using contact normal and platform-relative motion so underside and wall contacts cannot ground the player. Treat the experimental stable-v3.1.1 mover as a separate alternative consisting of `b2World_CollideMover`, `b2World_CastMover`, collision-plane assembly, `b2SolvePlanes`, and `b2ClipVector`, with the application owning steps, slopes, platform transport, persistent state, pushing, rotation, dynamic-body interaction, events, and replication. Compare both contracts on slopes, seams, steps, moving and rotating platforms, lifts, head impacts, drop-through, crowding, and rollback hashes, and move lift-joint anchor, motor, and break-policy design to `constraints-ragdolls-active-physics`.

8. **CCD:** Keep default continuous collision for dynamic bodies against static bodies, enable bullet mode only for sparse projectile bodies whose measured collision-pair envelope requires dynamic, kinematic, or dynamic targets, and do not enable bullets on every moving body. Bullet mode does not provide bullet-versus-bullet CCD, can interfere with joints, sensor shapes have no CCD, and continuous-collision contacts may produce ordinary events one step later. Use ray or shape casts for fast sensor crossings and compare bullet, ray, shape-cast, and hybrid projectile policies across declared speed, radius, target thickness, impact angle, target motion, substeps, event latency, and simultaneous-hit cases. Acceptance requires zero missed required impacts in the envelope, defined behavior outside it, bounded event latency, no lift-joint regression, and a measured p99 step cost that preserves the 3 ms budget in both dense-scene and fast-projectile matrices.

9. **Determinism and rollback:** Claim replay compatibility only for a pinned and qualified artifact with identical initial creation order, fixed tick, substeps, worker policy, build flags, inputs, commands, callbacks, event canonicalization, and application state, and treat any worker, compiler, CPU architecture, platform, or Box2D version change as a new compatibility lane requiring qualification. Official Box2D determinism targets 64-bit platforms, uses precise math on MSVC, disables floating-point contraction on Clang and GCC, covers x64 and ARM with custom trigonometry, and includes events in multithreaded ordering derived from creation order. Re-run the pinned official test at `1.0f / 60.0f`, 4 substeps, worker counts 1–5, expected sleep step 288, and expected hash `0x35467e1e`, while treating that result as engine evidence rather than application proof. Stable v3.1.1 has no public snapshot or rollback API, transforms omit contact, solver, sleep, joint, and application state, and no cross-version or arbitrary-build guarantee exists, so replay the complete ordered fixed-tick history from a reconstructible state, hash a durable-ID-keyed semantic projection every tick, compare players, platforms, bodies, velocities, sleep, joints, overlaps, contacts, commands, and gameplay state, and retain the first divergent tick with a structured field diff.

Keep broader work in the core workflows: fixed-loop, phase, and ownership architecture in `architecting-real-time-physics`; collision, contacts, one-way behavior, and CCD in `rigid-body-collision-contact`; lift constraints in `constraints-ragdolls-active-physics`; controller selection in `character-controller-movement`; rollback logs, windows, compatibility, and hashes in `networked-deterministic-physics`; adversarial reproduction in `debugging-testing-physics`; and profile, percentile, counter, and scaling analysis in `profiling-scaling-physics`.
